headline: High-risk default interaction: MinerU can feed extracted content into Open Interpreter, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and destructive-action paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU ingests untrusted PDFs/DOCX/XLSX and exposes MCP/API outputs; Open Interpreter has clipboard/stdin/file access and can execute code. If MinerU output is copied or piped into Open Interpreter, attacker-controlled document text can steer tool use. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is unsafe by default.
conditions: IF MinerU output is transferred into Open Interpreter via clipboard, stdin, or files
IF the document contains adversarial instructions embedded in OCR/text
mitigations: Disable copy/paste or piping between the tools
Review extracted text in a plain viewer before handing it to Open Interpreter
Use a provenance tag or wrapper that strips instructions from MinerU output
Run Open Interpreter in safe mode with confirmations enabled
requires-engineering: add content provenance filtering between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU touches PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, while Open Interpreter can read the entire user filesystem and send data to configured model providers. In a shared workspace, MinerU outputs may contain sensitive document contents that Open Interpreter can exfiltrate through prompts or provider calls. This is a default-dangerous pair unless tightly isolated.
conditions: IF MinerU processes sensitive documents in the same workspace Open Interpreter can read
IF Open Interpreter forwards context to a remote model provider
mitigations: Keep MinerU outputs in a separate directory Open Interpreter cannot read
Use local-only model providers for Open Interpreter
Redact sensitive fields before passing outputs onward
Restrict Open Interpreter to a minimal working folder
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the OS level

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MinerU is multi-threaded and can use MCP/API surfaces, while Open Interpreter has broad filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capabilities. If both operate on the same directory, concurrent writes and state changes can collide, corrupt files, or overwrite each other. The shared filesystem concurrency path is explicit in Open Interpreter and plausible for MinerU outputs.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF Open Interpreter runs while MinerU is still producing files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other mutates shared files
Avoid running both against the same git repository
Use file locks around shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted facts, tables, and OCR text that Open Interpreter can treat as input for actions. Open Interpreter then has authority to execute shell commands and modify files, so a mistaken extraction can cascade into destructive or incorrect operations. Because verification is not enabled by default, the pair can turn parsing errors into real-world actions.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter acts on MinerU-extracted facts without human verification
IF extracted OCR or table data is incomplete or wrong
mitigations: Require human review before any action based on MinerU output
Use a second validation step for critical fields
Limit Open Interpreter to read-only tasks until outputs are checked
Log source-to-action traceability for each step
requires-engineering: implement verification gates before execution

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline, but Open Interpreter can send context to configured model providers and read the whole filesystem. If regulated documents processed by MinerU are then exposed to Open Interpreter, residency and retention obligations can diverge. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from their combined data flow, not MinerU alone.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data processed by MinerU is forwarded into Open Interpreter
IF the configured provider retains prompts or stores logs outside required residency
mitigations: Use a local-only provider for Open Interpreter
Avoid forwarding regulated documents between agents
Check provider retention settings before use
Keep compliance-sensitive workloads in MinerU only
requires-engineering: document and enforce a data-flow policy
